SECTION 1 – SAFETY

1.1 GENERAL SAFETY
This machine has rotating parts that can cause serious injury. Only trained and authorised personnel may operate or maintain this centrifuge. Before any maintenance work, ensure that the machine is isolated from all energy sources and that the bowl has come to a complete stop.

1.2 LOCKOUT/TAGOUT (LOTO)
1. Notify the shift supervisor before isolating the centrifuge.
2. Close the inlet and outlet isolation valves.
3. Isolate the electrical supply at the main disconnect switch (MSD-104). Apply a lock and tag.
4. Isolate the hydraulic power unit (HPU-104) supply and lock out.
5. Verify zero energy: attempt a normal start from the local control panel. The machine must not start.
6. Wait for the bowl to stop rotating. Use the tachometer on the control panel to confirm zero speed.
7. If work is required inside the bowl or scroll, follow the confined space entry procedure (CSE-07) and use a mechanical bowl lock.

1.3 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
Minimum PPE for all work: safety glasses, safety boots, and hearing protection. When handling chemicals or cleaning agents, add chemical-resistant gloves and a face shield. When working inside the bowl, wear a full-body harness and attach the lanyard to the designated anchor point.

1.4 HOT WORK
Any welding, grinding, or use of open flame in the vicinity of the centrifuge requires a hot work permit. Refer to site procedure HWP-02.

SECTION 2 – OPERATING PROCEDURES

2.1 PRE-START CHECKS
1. Check that the feed tank level is above the low-level alarm set point.
2. Confirm that the flocculant make-up unit is in service and that the dosing pumps are primed.
3. Inspect the centrifuge area for leaks, loose parts, or obstructions.
4. Check the hydraulic oil level in HPU-104. Top up with ISO VG 46 oil if required.
5. Verify that the cooling water supply to the main bearings is open and that the flow rate is at least 8 L/min.
6. Check the condition of the feed hose and the discharge chute. Replace any worn or cracked sections.
7. Confirm that the control panel has no active alarms.

2.2 START-UP
1. Start the hydraulic power unit. Allow the oil temperature to reach at least 25 °C.
2. Start the centrifuge drive. The bowl will ramp up to the set speed.
3. Set the bowl speed to the required value for the current sludge type. Refer to the operating matrix in Appendix A of this manual.
4. When the bowl reaches the set speed and the vibration level is below 4.5 mm/s RMS, open the feed valve slowly.
5. Adjust the feed flow rate and flocculant dose to maintain the target cake dryness and centrate quality. Record the settings in the daily log.
6. Observe the torque reading. If the torque exceeds 85% of the rated value, reduce the feed rate immediately.

2.3 NORMAL OPERATION
The centrifuge is designed for continuous operation. The operator should check the unit at least every two hours and record the following: bowl speed, differential speed, torque, vibration, feed flow, flocculant dose, and centrate clarity. Any significant change from normal operating conditions should be reported to the shift supervisor.

The maximum operating speed for this machine is 3200 rpm. Do not exceed this speed under any circumstances. The normal operating speed is typically 2800–3100 rpm depending on the sludge feed characteristics.
After an emergency stop, do not restart the machine until the cause of the trip has been identified and rectified. The following checks must be completed before any restart:

1. Confirm that the vibration monitoring system has been reset and shows no active fault.
2. Check the main bearing temperatures and the hydraulic oil temperature for signs of overheating.
3. Inspect the feed line and flocculant line for blockages or air locks.
4. Verify that the discharge chute is clear and that the cake conveyor is running normally.
5. Contact the shift supervisor and the maintenance engineer before re-commissioning.

SECTION 4 – MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

Maintenance work on C-104 must be carried out by trained personnel only. The machine must be isolated, locked off, and tagged out before any maintenance activity begins. A permit to work is required for any task that involves entry into the bowl, work on the drive train, or work on the hydraulic system.

4.1 SCHEDULE SUMMARY

| Interval | Task | Reference |
|----------|------|-----------|
| Daily | Visual inspection for leaks, vibration, unusual noise; record bowl speed, torque, vibration, and feed flow | Section 4.2 |
| Weekly | Check hydraulic oil level and top up with ISO VG 46 as required; check cooling water flow; clean feed hose and discharge chute | Section 4.3 |
| Monthly | Grease main bearings; check V-belt tension and condition; check all pipe connections for tightness | Section 4.4 |
| Quarterly | Change hydraulic oil filter; check hydraulic oil for water or particulates; inspect feed zone for wear | Section 4.5 |
| 6-monthly | Change hydraulic oil; inspect bowl and scroll for wear; check differential speed gearbox oil level | Section 4.6 |
| Annually | Full strip-down inspection; replace all seals and O-rings; check bowl balance; recalibrate vibration and torque sensors | Section 4.7 |

4.2 DAILY CHECKS

1. Record bowl speed, differential speed, torque, vibration, feed flow, flocculant dose, and centrate clarity at the start of each shift and then every two hours during operation.
2. Listen for any unusual noise from the bowl, gearbox, or hydraulic unit.
3. Check for oil leaks from the hydraulic lines, the gearbox, and the main bearing housings.
4. Check the feed hose and discharge chute for wear or blockage.
5. Report any deviation from normal operating conditions to the shift supervisor.

4.3 WEEKLY CHECKS

1. Check the hydraulic oil level in HPU-104. Top up with ISO VG 46 oil if the level is below the minimum mark on the sight glass.
2. Check the cooling water flow to the main bearings. The flow rate must be at least 8 L/min.
3. Clean the feed hose and the discharge chute with clean water to remove any dried sludge.
4. Check the condition of the flexible connections on the feed and discharge lines. Replace any cracked or perished sections.

4.4 MONTHLY CHECKS

1. Grease the main bearings using the grease nipples provided. Use a lithium-based grease, NLGI grade 2. Apply 3–4 pumps of the grease gun per nipple.
2. Check the tension and condition of the V-belts on the bowl drive. The belts should deflect no more than 10 mm when pressed firmly at the midpoint between pulleys.
3. Check all pipe connections on the feed, flocculant, and discharge lines for tightness. Retighten any loose fittings.

4.5 QUARTERLY CHECKS

1. Replace the hydraulic oil filter in HPU-104. Record the filter part number and the date of replacement in the maintenance log.
2. Take a sample of the hydraulic oil and check for water content and particulate contamination. If the oil is contaminated, change the oil and investigate the cause.
3. Inspect the feed zone for wear. Check the feed pipe and the accelerator for scoring or erosion.

4.6 SIX-MONTHLY CHECKS
1. Inspect the main bearing housings for signs of overheating or fretting. Use a thermographic camera if available; record bearing housing temperatures in the maintenance log. Normal operating temperature is 55–70 °C at the outer housing surface.
2. Check the gearbox oil level and condition. Top up with the oil specified in Section 7.3 if required. If the oil appears milky or contains metallic particles, drain, flush, and refill, then investigate the cause before returning the machine to service.
3. Inspect the rotary union and its flexible hoses for signs of leakage or wear. Replace any suspect components.
4. Check the condition of the bowl scraper and the discharge ports. Remove any accumulated scale or debris.
5. Verify the calibration of the pressure gauges on the feed line and the hydraulic unit. Gauges that read more than 5% outside the reference standard must be replaced.
6. Check the condition of the vibration isolators under the machine base. Replace any isolator that shows cracking, permanent set, or loss of rubber-to-metal bond.

5.2 ANNUAL MAINTENANCE

1. Perform a full inspection of the bowl and the conveyor assembly. This inspection requires removal of the bowl shell and must only be carried out by trained personnel following the procedures in Section 8.
2. Measure the clearance between the conveyor flights and the bowl wall at four equally spaced points around the circumference. Record the measurements. The clearance must be within 0.5–1.5 mm. If any measurement is outside this range, adjust the conveyor position or replace the wear strips as described in Section 8.4.
3. Inspect the feed pipe and the accelerator for erosion, especially at the discharge end. Measure the wall thickness of the feed pipe at the wear points with an ultrasonic thickness gauge. Replace the pipe if the wall thickness is less than 3 mm at any point.
4. Drain, flush, and refill the gearbox with fresh oil. Record the oil type and quantity in the maintenance log.
5. Replace the hydraulic oil in HPU-104. Drain the old oil, replace the return filter and the pressure filter, clean the tank interior, and refill with ISO VG 46 oil.
6. Check the torque arm assembly for wear on the pivot pins and the bushings. Replace any worn parts.
7. Inspect the electrical connections inside the control panel. Retorque all power and control terminations to the values marked on the panel drawings. Check the condition of the cable glands and the door seals.
8. Test the operation of the emergency stop circuit and the safety interlocks. Refer to Section 9.2 for the test procedure.
9. Have the vibration sensors and the speed sensors recalibrated by the instrument contractor. Obtain a calibration certificate and file it with the maintenance log.

6.1 GENERAL
6.1 GENERAL

The troubleshooting tables in this section list the most common faults reported for the sludge thickener centrifuge C-104. The tables are arranged by symptom. Before carrying out any fault-finding, ensure that the machine is isolated and that the permit-to-work procedure described in Section 2.5 has been followed. Do not rely on the control panel indication alone; always verify the actual condition of the component concerned.

Where a fault condition is accompanied by an alarm or a trip, refer to the alarm schedule in Section 8.2 of the Control System Manual for the alarm set point and the reset procedure. If the fault cannot be cleared by the actions listed, contact the manufacturer’s service engineer. Record all faults and the actions taken in the maintenance log.

6.2 FAULT TABLE – HIGH VIBRATION

| | Worn main bearing | Measure bearing temperature and listen for noise. If suspect, replace the bearing. Refer to Section 7.4. |
| High vibration on the conveyor drive end | Conveyor scroll worn or damaged | Inspect the scroll flights through the inspection port. Replace the scroll if the flight edge is worn by more than 3 mm. |
| | Gearbox misalignment | Check the alignment of the gearbox to the centrifuge shaft. Realign if the offset exceeds 0.1 mm. |
| High vibration, both ends | Resonance with the support structure | Check the mounting bolts and the anti-vibration mounts. Tighten or replace as necessary. |

6.3 FAULT TABLE – HIGH MOTOR CURRENT

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Main drive motor current above 320 A for more than 30 seconds | Bowl overload due to high feed solids | Reduce the feed rate. Check the feed solids concentration. |
| | Differential speed set too low | Increase the differential speed by 1 rpm steps up to the maximum of 8 rpm. |
| | Mechanical binding inside the bowl | Stop the machine and carry out a manual rotation check. |
| Hydraulic pump motor current above the nameplate value | Hydraulic oil viscosity too high | Check the oil temperature. It must be above 25 °C before start-up. |
| | Pressure relief valve set too high | Check the pressure setting on HPU-104. It must be 120 bar. |

6.4 FAULT TABLE – POOR SLUDGE THICKENING

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Cake solids below 22% DS | Feed solids concentration too low | Check the feed concentration. If it is below 2.0% DS, the polymer dose must be adjusted. |
| | Polymer dose incorrect | Carry out a jar test and reset the polymer dose. Record the new dose in the log. |
| | Differential speed too high | Reduce the differential speed in 0.5 rpm steps. |
| | Weir plate set too high | Check the weir plate setting against the drawing in Appendix A. |
| Centrate contains excessive suspended solids | Polymer flocculation poor | Check the polymer make-up concentration and the mixing time. |
| | Feed flow rate above the design maximum | Reduce the feed flow rate. The maximum design flow is 85 m³/h. |
| | Conveyor scroll worn | Inspect the scroll flights. Replace if worn. |

6.5 FAULT TABLE – LEAKS

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Oil leak from the gearbox | Gearbox oil seal worn | Replace the oil seal. Refer to Section 7.3. |
| | Gearbox breather blocked | Remove and clean the breather. |
| Water leak from the feed pipe connection | Loose flange or damaged gasket | Tighten the flange bolts evenly. Replace the gasket if damaged. |
| Hydraulic oil leak from the HPU | Loose fitting or damaged hose | Check all fittings and hoses. Replace any damaged hose. |

Level is monitored by two independent radar transmitters (NKWTW-LT-101 and NKWTW-LT-102) which provide inputs to the SCADA system for level control and alarm management. The overflow weir is set at a level corresponding to a stored volume of 120 ML and discharges to the river via a consented outfall. The scour pipework includes a motorised valve and discharges to the site drainage system.

SECTION 1 – SAFETY

1.1 GENERAL SAFETY
This machine has rotating parts that can cause serious injury. Only trained and authorised personnel may operate or maintain this centrifuge. Before any maintenance work, ensure that the machine is isolated from all energy sources and that the bowl has come to a complete stop.

1.2 LOCKOUT/TAGOUT (LOTO)
1. Notify the shift supervisor before isolating the centrifuge.
2. Close the inlet and outlet isolation valves.
3. Isolate the electrical supply at the main disconnect switch (MSD-104). Apply a lock and tag.
4. Isolate the hydraulic power unit (HPU-104) supply and lock out.
5. Verify zero energy: attempt a normal start from the local control panel. The machine must not start.
6. Wait for the bowl to stop rotating. Use the tachometer on the control panel to confirm zero speed.
7. If work is required inside the bowl or scroll, follow the confined space entry procedure (CSE-07) and use a mechanical bowl lock.

1.3 PERSONAL PROTECTIVE EQUIPMENT (PPE)
Minimum PPE for all work: safety glasses, safety boots, and hearing protection. When handling chemicals or cleaning agents, add chemical-resistant gloves and a face shield. When working inside the bowl, wear a full-body harness and attach the lanyard to the designated anchor point.

1.4 HOT WORK
Any welding, grinding, or use of open flame in the vicinity of the centrifuge requires a hot work permit. Refer to site procedure HWP-02.

Sludge Thickener Centrifuge C-104 maximum_operating_speed_rpm 3200 rpm. Record status: current.

SECTION 2 – OPERATING PROCEDURES

2.1 PRE-START CHECKS
1. Check that the feed tank level is above the low-level alarm set point.
2. Confirm that the flocculant make-up unit is in service and that the dosing pumps are primed.
3. Inspect the centrifuge area for leaks, loose parts, or obstructions.
4. Check the hydraulic oil level in HPU-104. Top up with ISO VG 46 oil if required.
5. Verify that the cooling water supply to the main bearings is open and that the flow rate is at least 8 L/min.
6. Check the condition of the feed hose and the discharge chute. Replace any worn or cracked sections.
7. Confirm that the control panel has no active alarms.

2.2 START-UP
1. Start the hydraulic power unit. Allow the oil temperature to reach at least 25 °C.
2. Start the centrifuge drive. The bowl will ramp up to the set speed.
3. Set the bowl speed to the required value for the current sludge type. Refer to the operating matrix in Appendix A of this manual.
4. When the bowl reaches the set speed and the vibration level is below 4.5 mm/s RMS, open the feed valve slowly.
5. Adjust the feed flow rate and flocculant dose to maintain the target cake dryness and centrate quality. Record the settings in the daily log.
6. Observe the torque reading. If the torque exceeds 85% of the rated value, reduce the feed rate immediately.

2.3 NORMAL OPERATION
The centrifuge is designed for continuous operation. The operator should check the unit at least every two hours and record the following: bowl speed, differential speed, torque, vibration, feed flow, flocculant dose, and centrate clarity. Any significant change from normal operating conditions should be reported to the shift supervisor.

The maximum operating speed for this machine is 3200 rpm. Do not exceed this speed under any circumstances. The normal operating speed is typically 2800–3100 rpm depending on the sludge feed characteristics.

documents.content:
After an emergency stop, do not restart the machine until the cause of the trip has been identified and rectified. The following checks must be completed before any restart:

1. Confirm that the vibration monitoring system has been reset and shows no active fault.
2. Check the main bearing temperatures and the hydraulic oil temperature for signs of overheating.
3. Inspect the feed line and flocculant line for blockages or air locks.
4. Verify that the discharge chute is clear and that the cake conveyor is running normally.
5. Contact the shift supervisor and the maintenance engineer before re-commissioning.

SECTION 4 – MAINTENANCE SCHEDULE

Maintenance work on C-104 must be carried out by trained personnel only. The machine must be isolated, locked off, and tagged out before any maintenance activity begins. A permit to work is required for any task that involves entry into the bowl, work on the drive train, or work on the hydraulic system.

4.1 SCHEDULE SUMMARY

| Interval | Task | Reference |
|----------|------|-----------|
| Daily | Visual inspection for leaks, vibration, unusual noise; record bowl speed, torque, vibration, and feed flow | Section 4.2 |
| Weekly | Check hydraulic oil level and top up with ISO VG 46 as required; check cooling water flow; clean feed hose and discharge chute | Section 4.3 |
| Monthly | Grease main bearings; check V-belt tension and condition; check all pipe connections for tightness | Section 4.4 |
| Quarterly | Change hydraulic oil filter; check hydraulic oil for water or particulates; inspect feed zone for wear | Section 4.5 |
| 6-monthly | Change hydraulic oil; inspect bowl and scroll for wear; check differential speed gearbox oil level | Section 4.6 |
| Annually | Full strip-down inspection; replace all seals and O-rings; check bowl balance; recalibrate vibration and torque sensors | Section 4.7 |

4.2 DAILY CHECKS

1. Record bowl speed, differential speed, torque, vibration, feed flow, flocculant dose, and centrate clarity at the start of each shift and then every two hours during operation.
2. Listen for any unusual noise from the bowl, gearbox, or hydraulic unit.
3. Check for oil leaks from the hydraulic lines, the gearbox, and the main bearing housings.
4. Check the feed hose and discharge chute for wear or blockage.
5. Report any deviation from normal operating conditions to the shift supervisor.

High Lift Pump P-301 design_flow_rate_m3_per_hour 1250 m3/h. Record status: current.

4.3 WEEKLY CHECKS

1. Check the hydraulic oil level in HPU-104. Top up with ISO VG 46 oil if the level is below the minimum mark on the sight glass.
2. Check the cooling water flow to the main bearings. The flow rate must be at least 8 L/min.
3. Clean the feed hose and the discharge chute with clean water to remove any dried sludge.
4. Check the condition of the flexible connections on the feed and discharge lines. Replace any cracked or perished sections.

4.4 MONTHLY CHECKS

1. Grease the main bearings using the grease nipples provided. Use a lithium-based grease, NLGI grade 2. Apply 3–4 pumps of the grease gun per nipple.
2. Check the tension and condition of the V-belts on the bowl drive. The belts should deflect no more than 10 mm when pressed firmly at the midpoint between pulleys.
3. Check all pipe connections on the feed, flocculant, and discharge lines for tightness. Retighten any loose fittings.

4.5 QUARTERLY CHECKS

1. Replace the hydraulic oil filter in HPU-104. Record the filter part number and the date of replacement in the maintenance log.
2. Take a sample of the hydraulic oil and check for water content and particulate contamination. If the oil is contaminated, change the oil and investigate the cause.
3. Inspect the feed zone for wear. Check the feed pipe and the accelerator for scoring or erosion.

4.6 SIX-MONTHLY CHECKS

documents.title: Maintenance Manual MM-104 – Sludge Thickener Centrifuge C-104
documents.content:
1. Inspect the main bearing housings for signs of overheating or fretting. Use a thermographic camera if available; record bearing housing temperatures in the maintenance log. Normal operating temperature is 55–70 °C at the outer housing surface.
2. Check the gearbox oil level and condition. Top up with the oil specified in Section 7.3 if required. If the oil appears milky or contains metallic particles, drain, flush, and refill, then investigate the cause before returning the machine to service.
3. Inspect the rotary union and its flexible hoses for signs of leakage or wear. Replace any suspect components.
4. Check the condition of the bowl scraper and the discharge ports. Remove any accumulated scale or debris.
5. Verify the calibration of the pressure gauges on the feed line and the hydraulic unit. Gauges that read more than 5% outside the reference standard must be replaced.
6. Check the condition of the vibration isolators under the machine base. Replace any isolator that shows cracking, permanent set, or loss of rubber-to-metal bond.

5.2 ANNUAL MAINTENANCE

1. Perform a full inspection of the bowl and the conveyor assembly. This inspection requires removal of the bowl shell and must only be carried out by trained personnel following the procedures in Section 8.
2. Measure the clearance between the conveyor flights and the bowl wall at four equally spaced points around the circumference. Record the measurements. The clearance must be within 0.5–1.5 mm. If any measurement is outside this range, adjust the conveyor position or replace the wear strips as described in Section 8.4.
3. Inspect the feed pipe and the accelerator for erosion, especially at the discharge end. Measure the wall thickness of the feed pipe at the wear points with an ultrasonic thickness gauge. Replace the pipe if the wall thickness is less than 3 mm at any point.
4. Drain, flush, and refill the gearbox with fresh oil. Record the oil type and quantity in the maintenance log.
5. Replace the hydraulic oil in HPU-104. Drain the old oil, replace the return filter and the pressure filter, clean the tank interior, and refill with ISO VG 46 oil.
6. Check the torque arm assembly for wear on the pivot pins and the bushings. Replace any worn parts.
7. Inspect the electrical connections inside the control panel. Retorque all power and control terminations to the values marked on the panel drawings. Check the condition of the cable glands and the door seals.
8. Test the operation of the emergency stop circuit and the safety interlocks. Refer to Section 9.2 for the test procedure.
9. Have the vibration sensors and the speed sensors recalibrated by the instrument contractor. Obtain a calibration certificate and file it with the maintenance log.

5.3 LUBRICATION SCHEDULE

The following table summarises the lubrication points, the lubricant type, and the frequency.

| Item | Lubricant | Frequency | Method |
|------|-----------|-----------|--------|
| Main bearings | Lithium grease, NLGI grade 2 | Monthly | Grease gun, 3–4 pumps per nipple |
| Gearbox | See Section 7.3 | Annually | Drain, flush, refill |
| Hydraulic system (HPU-104) | ISO VG 46 oil | Annually | Drain, flush, refill |
| Feed pipe wear strips | Molybdenum disulphide paste | Annually | Apply thin coat to contact faces |

Note: Do not mix different brands or grades of grease in the same bearing. If the grease type is changed, purge the old grease from the bearing before applying the new grease.

SECTION 6 – TROUBLESHOOTING

6.1 GENERAL

documents.content:
6.1 GENERAL

The troubleshooting tables in this section list the most common faults reported for the sludge thickener centrifuge C-104. The tables are arranged by symptom. Before carrying out any fault-finding, ensure that the machine is isolated and that the permit-to-work procedure described in Section 2.5 has been followed. Do not rely on the control panel indication alone; always verify the actual condition of the component concerned.

Where a fault condition is accompanied by an alarm or a trip, refer to the alarm schedule in Section 8.2 of the Control System Manual for the alarm set point and the reset procedure. If the fault cannot be cleared by the actions listed, contact the manufacturer’s service engineer. Record all faults and the actions taken in the maintenance log.

6.2 FAULT TABLE – HIGH VIBRATION

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| High vibration on the main bearing housing, left side | Feed solids concentration above the design limit | Check the feed sludge concentration. If it exceeds 4.5% DS, reduce the feed rate or dilute the feed. |
| | Imbalance of the bowl due to uneven solids build-up | Run the flush cycle as described in Section 3.7. If the vibration persists, stop the machine and inspect the bowl interior. |
| | Worn main bearing | Measure bearing temperature and listen for noise. If suspect, replace the bearing. Refer to Section 7.4. |
| High vibration on the conveyor drive end | Conveyor scroll worn or damaged | Inspect the scroll flights through the inspection port. Replace the scroll if the flight edge is worn by more than 3 mm. |
| | Gearbox misalignment | Check the alignment of the gearbox to the centrifuge shaft. Realign if the offset exceeds 0.1 mm. |
| High vibration, both ends | Resonance with the support structure | Check the mounting bolts and the anti-vibration mounts. Tighten or replace as necessary. |

6.3 FAULT TABLE – HIGH MOTOR CURRENT

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Main drive motor current above 320 A for more than 30 seconds | Bowl overload due to high feed solids | Reduce the feed rate. Check the feed solids concentration. |
| | Differential speed set too low | Increase the differential speed by 1 rpm steps up to the maximum of 8 rpm. |
| | Mechanical binding inside the bowl | Stop the machine and carry out a manual rotation check. |
| Hydraulic pump motor current above the nameplate value | Hydraulic oil viscosity too high | Check the oil temperature. It must be above 25 °C before start-up. |
| | Pressure relief valve set too high | Check the pressure setting on HPU-104. It must be 120 bar. |

6.4 FAULT TABLE – POOR SLUDGE THICKENING

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Cake solids below 22% DS | Feed solids concentration too low | Check the feed concentration. If it is below 2.0% DS, the polymer dose must be adjusted. |
| | Polymer dose incorrect | Carry out a jar test and reset the polymer dose. Record the new dose in the log. |
| | Differential speed too high | Reduce the differential speed in 0.5 rpm steps. |
| | Weir plate set too high | Check the weir plate setting against the drawing in Appendix A. |
| Centrate contains excessive suspended solids | Polymer flocculation poor | Check the polymer make-up concentration and the mixing time. |
| | Feed flow rate above the design maximum | Reduce the feed flow rate. The maximum design flow is 85 m³/h. |
| | Conveyor scroll worn | Inspect the scroll flights. Replace if worn. |

6.5 FAULT TABLE – LEAKS

| Symptom | Possible Cause | Check / Action |
|---------|----------------|----------------|
| Oil leak from the gearbox | Gearbox oil seal worn | Replace the oil seal. Refer to Section 7.3. |
| | Gearbox breather blocked | Remove and clean the breather. |
| Water leak from the feed pipe connection | Loose flange or damaged gasket | Tighten the flange bolts evenly. Replace the gasket if damaged. |
| Hydraulic oil leak from the HPU | Loose fitting or damaged hose | Check all fittings and hoses. Replace any damaged hose. |

ENTRY SEL-2026-03-006
Date/Time: 04/03/2026, 09:15 GMT
Asset: Site Drainage / Interceptor
Issue: Routine weekly inspection of the site drainage system identified a light sheen on the surface of the water in the oil/water interceptor (Interceptor I-2), located adjacent to the main workshop. The sheen was estimated to cover approximately 2 m² of the interceptor surface. No free oil was visible. The interceptor discharge point was checked; no sheen was visible in the final discharge channel. The site discharge consent (EA/NK/2015/0042) requires that there be no visible oil sheen in the discharge. The incident was logged as a potential breach of consent conditions, pending verification.

Action Taken: The interceptor inlet was checked – no obvious source of oil identified. The workshop bunded area and vehicle washdown area were inspected; no spills or leaks found. A sample of the interceptor water was taken for laboratory analysis (oil-in-water). The interceptor weir and coalescing media were inspected – no excessive sludge or blockage noted. The interceptor was not isolated as the sheen was considered minor and the discharge was clear. The Environment Agency was not notified at this stage; decision to be reviewed once sample results are available. The oil/water interceptor maintenance contractor was contacted and asked to attend to inspect the unit and carry out a full clean-out if required. The sample was sent to the laboratory with a request for a 24-hour turnaround.

ENTRY SEL-2026-03-007
Date/Time: 05/03/2026, 11:30 GMT
Asset: Clarifier No. 2 – Bridge Drive
Issue: During routine visual inspection of Clarifier No. 2, the bridge drive motor was noted to be running at a higher than normal temperature. The motor casing temperature was measured at 78°C using a thermal imaging camera. Normal operating temperature for this motor is 55–65°C. The motor is a 5.5 kW, 415V, 3-phase unit, driving the clarifier bridge via a worm gearbox. No abnormal noise or vibration was detected. The clarifier was in service at the time.

The gearbox was topped up with the correct grade of oil (Shell Omala S2 G 220). The motor cooling fan was checked – clear of debris. The motor was run for a further 30 minutes and the temperature was re-checked – 68°C and falling. The motor was left in service. The gearbox oil level to be checked again after 24 hours. Thermal imaging of the motor to be repeated during the next routine condition monitoring round.

The screen was then returned to service at 10:40 and the differential pressure returned to normal (0.15 bar). The automatic raking cycle was observed for one full cycle – operating correctly. Asset: Site Drainage – Interceptor
Issue: During a routine site walk, a light sheen was observed on the water surface in the interceptor chamber adjacent to the chemical storage area. The interceptor serves the site drainage system and is designed to remove hydrocarbons before discharge to the foul sewer. The sheen was estimated to cover approximately 10% of the chamber surface. ENTRY SEL-2026-03-011
Date/Time: 09/03/2026, 11:50 GMT
Asset: High Lift Pump No. 3 – Gland Seal
Issue: At approximately 11:30, the duty high lift pump (No. 3) was noted to be leaking from the gland area. The leak was estimated at approximately 2–3 drops per second. The pump is a 90 kW, 415V, vertical spindle pump. The gland seal is a packed gland type. The pump was in service at the time. The gland was adjusted previously on 24/02/2026 (see entry SEL-2026-02-018). The leak rate is above the normal acceptable limit of 1 drop per second.

The gland area to be checked at the next shift change.
